Hi Hannah —

Thanks for the call this morning. Starline is generally comfortable with an auto-renew model, but procurement needs two confirmations before we can move to legal: (1) a rolling notice window (so the renewal date can move with usage start dates across sub-accounts) and (2) a clear termination-for-convenience cushion for the first 12 months (we'd want a known fee instead of open-ended liability).

I've attached our annotated order form and a short redline (Starline_Redlines_v1.pdf). Can your team propose exact clause language for the rolling window and the termination fee mechanics? Also please confirm if a 60-day notice window is workable for you.

Procurement contact is procurement@starline.io — they will own contracting.

Thanks,
Samantha Holt
Director, Strategic Procurement
Starline Health

Hi Samantha —

Appreciate the clear asks and the PDF. Short answers up front: yes, we can support a rolling renewal window and we can propose a termination-for-convenience structure with a capped termination fee for year 1.

Next steps I propose:
- Our legal team will publish suggested contract language for the rolling window (two variants: 60-day rolling notice; and 90-day rolling notice).
- Ben will propose the termination-for-convenience fee mechanics (flat % of remaining committed year vs. 1x monthly run-rate).
- We'll return a single tracked document for your review by EOD tomorrow.

Attaching our internal preliminary redline (redlines_marked.docx) so you can see where we'll put the clauses. Can you confirm whether Starline needs the rolling window at the account-level or per-subaccount? That will determine the exact language.

Hannah / Markus —

I took a first pass on legal language. Two points we should be intentional about:
1) Cure period: add a 30-day cure period for termination-for-convenience triggers tied to non-payment or material breach to avoid accidental chargebacks with rolling windows.
2) Fee mechanics: prefer a fixed capped fee (example: termination fee equal to 25% of the remaining committed contract value or a single-month run-rate, whichever is lower). That gives Starline predictability and limits Redwood's downside.

Draft snips (to be pasted under Term/Termination):
"Termination for Convenience: Either party may terminate the Order Form for convenience upon providing at least sixty (60) days' prior written notice to the other party. If Customer terminates for convenience within the first twelve (12) months following the Effective Date, Customer will pay a termination fee equal to the lesser of (a) twenty-five percent (25%) of the remaining unpaid fees under the Order Form as of the effective date of termination, or (b) one (1) times the then-current monthly run-rate for the Services."

"Rolling Renewal: The renewal term for the Services shall automatically renew for successive periods unless Customer provides written notice at least sixty (60) days prior to the then-current Renewal Date. For multi-subaccount deployments, the Renewal Date will be determined per subaccount based on the respective Service activation date unless Parties agree in writing to a consolidated account-level Renewal Date."

I've attached a tracked-changes Word file with these edits (legal_redline_track_changes.docx). If procurement wants an alternate (e.g., 90-day notice) we should present both and flag the SLO/ops impacts.

Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Legal Operations, Redwood Inference

Happy to align on precise wording.

Samantha / procurement team —

Thanks for the confirmation. Below are the two drafted clauses; I've pasted them into the order form and attached a final tracked document and a sample termination schedule for modeling. If everything looks good on your end we can route to DocuSign and aim to finalize next week.

-- Proposed clauses (for insertion under Section 3: Term; Section 8: Termination):

1) Rolling Renewal (insert under Term)
"The Services shall commence on the Service activation date for each subaccount and shall continue for the initial term specified in the applicable Order Form. Unless Customer gives written notice at least sixty (60) days prior to the then-current Renewal Date for the applicable subaccount, the Term for that subaccount will automatically renew for successive periods equal to the initial term. For clarity, Renewal Dates are calculated per subaccount based on the activation date unless the Parties expressly designate a consolidated Renewal Date in writing."

2) Termination for Convenience (insert under Termination)
"Either party may terminate the Order Form for convenience upon providing at least sixty (60) days' prior written notice to the other party. If Customer terminates for convenience within the first twelve (12) months following the Effective Date, Customer will pay a termination fee equal to the lesser of: (a) twenty-five percent (25%) of the remaining unpaid fees under the Order Form as of the effective date of termination; or (b) one (1) times the then-current monthly run-rate for the Services. Prior to any termination taking effect, Customer will have a thirty (30) day cure period following written notice to remedy any non-payment or other material breach that is the subject of the termination."
